# Results — Study 434 (DEMA & TEMA) on real daily SPY

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One rule — **long when the close
is above its moving average, flat otherwise** — run identically on a plain **SMA**, an **EMA**,
and the "less-lag" **DEMA** (Mulloy, 1994) and **TEMA**, all at a **50-day window**, with one
documented execution lag (signal at the close of *t*, return of *t+1*) and one-way costs ×
turnover. Raced on **net, excess-of-cash Sharpe** against buy-and-hold and against the plain
SMA. As-of **2026-05-31** (the partial June 2026 month is dropped); history back to 2005-01-03.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n bars | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPY | 2005-01-03 to 2026-05-29 | 5,385 | `0f42b216fe70` |

Yahoo! Finance daily bars (`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True` → total-return-ish adjusted close).
Cache-first under `_cache/`; the reproducible core never touches the network on a cache hit.

## The Sharpe race — net, excess-of-cash (n = 50, one-way cost = 2 bps)

Same rule, only the moving-average line changes. **Buy-and-hold net excess Sharpe = +0.645.**

| MA line | gross Sharpe | **net Sharpe** | Sharpe − B&H | HAC *t* (excess vs B&H) | turnover/yr | time in mkt |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SMA (plain) | +0.568 | **+0.536** | −0.109 | **−2.30** | 16.9 | 69.3% |
| EMA | +0.675 | **+0.641** | −0.004 | −1.86 | 18.2 | 72.1% |
| **DEMA** | +0.483 | **+0.420** | −0.225 | −2.79 | 34.2 | 56.3% |
| **TEMA** | +0.308 | **+0.240** | −0.405 | −3.49 | 38.9 | 52.1% |

- The "improved" lines are the **worst**: TEMA nets **+0.240**, DEMA **+0.420**, both below the
  plain SMA (**+0.536**) and EMA (**+0.641**) — and all four below **just holding SPY (+0.645)**.
- Every rule's daily *excess-over-buy-and-hold* HAC *t* is **negative**. Nothing clears the
  **+2** bar — there is no real timing edge to attribute to *any* of these lines.
- DEMA/TEMA trade **~2× more** (34–39 vs 17 round-trips/yr): the lag-cancellation re-injects
  high-frequency noise, which the threshold rule turns into whipsaw.

## The paired test — does the "less lag" line beat the plain SMA it claims to improve?

Daily *X-minus-SMA* net return, HAC *t* on the difference:

| Pair | ann mean | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| DEMA − SMA | −1.22%/yr | −0.64 |
| TEMA − SMA | −3.00%/yr | −1.25 |

The lag fix makes the rule **worse**, not better (both deltas negative; TEMA's drag is the larger).

## The permutation null — is the timing better than a random schedule?

A circular **block permutation** (block = 21 d) of the realised position schedule — same fraction
of long days, same block autocorrelation, random *timing* — recomputed 5,000× against the same
return tape:

| Rule | observed net Sharpe | placebo mean | *p* (random ≥ observed) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| DEMA | +0.420 | +0.433 | 0.527 |
| TEMA | +0.240 | +0.406 | **0.876** |

A random long/flat schedule with TEMA's activity level **beats TEMA's actual timing 88% of the
time**. The timing adds nothing over noise.

## Could you trade it? — cost sweep (net Sharpe, n = 50)

| one-way cost | SMA | DEMA | TEMA |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +0.568 | +0.483 | +0.308 |
| 2.0 bps | +0.536 | +0.420 | +0.240 |
| 5.0 bps | +0.489 | +0.324 | +0.137 |
| 10.0 bps | +0.410 | +0.165 | −0.033 |

TEMA falls fastest (most turnover) and crosses zero by ~10 bps — but it is **already behind at
zero cost** (+0.308 vs the SMA's +0.568). The Mirage doesn't need costs; they just make it
obvious faster. None of the lines beats buy-and-hold at any cost level.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN see an edge (and DEMA/TEMA still lose)

Deterministic synthetic tape (`data.synthetic_panel`) with a *planted* slow OU trend (knob
`edge`), n = 50, 2 bps. The SMA rule must light up when an edge exists:

| planted edge | buy-and-hold | SMA rule | TEMA rule |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 (martingale) | +0.636 | +0.605 | +0.501 |
| 1.0 | −0.985 | **+2.369** | −0.260 |
| 2.0 | −2.183 | **+4.035** | −0.535 |

When a real trend is planted, the SMA rule banks it (Sharpe to **+4.0** while buy-and-hold
craters to **−2.2**) — the harness is a faithful trend detector. And even there, **TEMA goes
negative**: its noise-sensitivity throws away the very trend it was built to catch sooner. The
less-lag line is a liability *with or without* a real signal. (This is a machinery proof — it
never backs the real-tape stamp.)

## Verdict

- **Signal — `NONE`.** Buy-and-hold nets +0.645; every MA rule lands below it with a **negative**
  excess-over-B&H HAC *t* (SMA −2.30, EMA −1.86, DEMA −2.79, TEMA −3.49). Nothing clears +2.
- **Tradability — `MIRAGE`.** TEMA net Sharpe +0.240 < SMA +0.536 < B&H +0.645, at ~2× turnover;
  its timing also loses to a random schedule (placebo *p* = 0.88). Nothing to deploy.
- **"Worth it?" — `BUSTED`.** The lag-cancellation algebra is real, but TEMA−SMA runs −3.0%/yr
  (HAC *t* = −1.25) and DEMA−SMA −1.22%/yr (−0.64). Less lag bought a strictly worse rule.
